slides.title: Isosceles Triangle Theorem
slides.html:
Isosceles Triangle Theorem

I can prove that base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

geo.title: Isosceles Triangle Theorem
geo.target: I can prove that base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

slides.title: Get started
slides.html:
Paper folding: cut out an isosceles triangle, fold so the equal legs match, and see which angles land on each other. Then turn the triangle upside down and ask again.

  • I can find the base angles of an isosceles triangle in any orientation by looking opposite the equal legs.
  • I can follow the bisector-and-SAS proof of Theorem 9 and solve base-angle equations without using the 180 degree sum.

geo.title: Get started
geo.body:
Paper folding: cut out an isosceles triangle, fold so the equal legs match, and see which angles land on each other. Then turn the triangle upside down and ask again.

  • I can find the base angles of an isosceles triangle in any orientation by looking opposite the equal legs.
  • I can follow the bisector-and-SAS proof of Theorem 9 and solve base-angle equations without using the 180 degree sum.

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html: the base angles are the angles opposite the equal sides, wherever the triangle points.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
Proof of Theorem 9 (adapted from Jacobs p. 158).

Read the worked steps
StepReason
In triangle ABC, AB = AC.Given.
Draw AD, the bisector of angle A, meeting BC at D.Every angle has a bisector (Protractor Postulate).
Angle BAD ≅ angle CAD.Definition of bisector.
AD = AD.A segment equals itself.
Triangle ABD ≅ triangle ACD.SAS.
Angle B ≅ angle C.CPCTC.

slides.title: Worked example
slides.html:
Find the base angles (original problem).

Read the worked steps
StepReason
AB = AC, angle B = (3x + 5) degrees, angle C = (5x - 17) degrees.Given. The figure is turned sideways.
3x + 5 = 5x - 17.Theorem 9: base angles are equal.
2x = 22, so x = 11.Solve.
Both base angles are 38 degrees.Substitute: 3(11) + 5 = 38.
We stop here. We don't find the top angle yet.The 180 degree angle sum comes in Unit 5.

slides.title: Common mistake
slides.html:
Jordan says the base angles are always the bottom ones.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Find and fix the error

The base angles are not 'the bottom ones'. They are the angles across from the equal sides, wherever the triangle points. And no 180 degree math until Unit 5.

slides.title: Practice 2
slides.html:
Base angles are 2x + 7 and 4x - 9. Find x.

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

2x + 7 = 4x - 9, so 2x = 16 and x = 8. Each angle is 23.

Reveal second check

2(8) + 7 = 23 and 4(8) - 9 = 23.

slides.html:

Try it on paper first, then reveal.

Reveal solution

Angle B = angle C. We can't find their size yet.

Reveal second check

Theorem 9 says the angles are equal. It says nothing about a sum.
